title: Augmented, not artificial
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Would you be proud to put out the work an AI did for you?
I asked: how can AI be used in a wrong way, and how in a right way? A student said: taking credit for AI's work without disclosing it, or acknowledging to clients that AI is part of the process.

Our company policy, the student said, is that every employee must find a way to implement AI responsibly in their daily tasks. We treat AI as augmented intelligence, not artificial intelligence. The human who puts out the work is ultimately responsible for its credibility, correctness, accuracy and quality, as if they did it themselves.

As a former literature teacher, I said, I remember talking about plagiarism. Students copied from search results, and I could not tell whether it was them or the search engine. Are you doing harm to yourself by pasting seven articles together, or doing yourself justice by reading other views and synthesizing them into your own thought? Where is the line?
A student said: if you can't articulate it, defend it and debate it as you would your own thought process, then you are plagiarizing. You are letting somebody else do your work.

I set a case: you offer a company one blog post a day for search engine optimization, the AI writes it and you send it every day, and you get paid. Is that fair business? A student said: dishonest if you are not proofing it. Another said: it is all about honesty and transparency.

A student said it doesn't work in every industry: a doctor is writing about someone's health, and a blog for a sports equipment company has nothing to do with anyone's safety. If it's not work you would be proud to put out as your own, you shouldn't put it out.
AI is meant to be a tool, the student said. If you let it be a replacement, it will be a replacement.
What do you tell a client about how the work was made?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write where you use AI in your work.
Write what you tell the people you serve about it.
Write the test: can you articulate, defend and debate the work?
Write one task you will not hand over.
Write what you would be proud to put your name on.

check.q: How did the student's company treat AI?
What was the student's test for plagiarism?
choices: Whether you can articulate, defend and debate it

check.q: What did the student say AI is meant to be?

recap: Use AI as a tool. Say how the work was made. Put your name only on what you can defend.
